correctness.rationale: For each infinite κ, any two κ-sized abelian groups embed into their direct product A×B, of size κ, so the subobject embeddability frame is reflexive/transitive/directed and validates S4.2. Berger–Block–Löwe supply arbitrary finite independent FIRST-ORDER control sets β_p=∃x≠0(px=0) and σ_q=∀x∃y(qy=x) on ALL abelian groups. For any starting A of size κ and any compatible pattern, take their witnessing extension B≥A; by ordinary downward Löwenheim–Skolem for group language with parameter set A obtain elementary subgroup C≺B containing A with κ≤|C|≤κ+ℵ0=κ. Subgroup inclusion A≤C and elementarity preserve every first-order button/switch truth value; hence the same finite independent patterns exist within exact κ, proving ML_{LGr}(A_κ)⊆S4.2 by the control theorem. The directed lower bound and valuation-language monotonicity sandwich give equality for all adequate languages. An infinite κ is essential; this does not prove modal preservation for arbitrary higher-order controls.

originality.rationale: Prior Berger–Christensen Block–Löwe 2023 proves S4.2 for the class of all abelian groups, not exact fixed κ, and its full-function-group constructions can enlarge cardinality. Saveliev–Shapirovsky 2020 gives modal downward-LS size-≤κ results but not exact-layer subgroup logic merely by restriction. Hałapacz 2026's full ten-page paper treats ratchets and an application to infinite linear-order theories, not abelian groups or fixed-κ transfer. The submitted cardinality-correction of first-order independent controls is short and perhaps folklore, but the precise exact-κ robustness statement is not a corollary of bounded-cardinal modal equality alone and is not stated in checked primary sources.
residual_risks: A prior Master's thesis by Berger (2018) or unpublished notes may contain exact-layer corollary, not fully ruled out.
The new argument is a short consequence of existing independent controls plus standard downward Löwenheim–Skolem, so novelty may be folklore.
Does not transfer arbitrary non-first-order control properties or finite cardinalities.

value.rationale: The known modal characterization of all abelian groups leaves open whether it survives fixing the exact infinite cardinality of each possible world; restriction can introduce new modal validities. The elementary-submodel transfer shows the full S4.2 richness persists already among countable abelian groups and uniformly at every infinite size. This gives a useful stability/robustness lemma bridging potentialist frames and model-theoretic cardinal arithmetic, with a complete all-κ proof.

limitations: Only infinite κ and abelian-group embeddability; no all-groups or finite-layer claim.
